title: Simplex-lift criterion for a right-anodyne decomposition inclusion
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, ordinary nerves and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and right anodyne maps of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, $I$ a small ordinary category, and $F:I\to\mathrm{sSet}_{/K}$ a functor, written $a\mapsto(\pi_a:K_a\to K)$; its arrows are simplicial maps commuting with the maps to $K$. Let $K_F$ be the decomposition simplicial set specified in [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones]: an $n$-simplex has a cut $-1\leq i\leq n$, a lower simplex $\sigma:\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,i\}}\to K$ when $i\geq0$, an upper chain $a_{i+1}\to\cdots\to a_n$ when $i<n$, and lifts $\sigma_j:\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,i\}}\to K_{a_j}$ for $j>i$, with $\pi_{a_j}\sigma_j=\sigma$ and $F(a_j\to a_k)\sigma_j=\sigma_k$. The all-upper case is a simplex of $N(I)$ and the all-lower case is a simplex of $K$; operators restrict or repeat the two blocks and compose the arrows, retaining the pure simplex when a block disappears. For every simplex $z\in K_m$, define the ordinary category $I_z$ to have objects $(a,w)$ with $w\in(K_a)_m$ and $\pi_a(w)=z$, and arrows $(a,w)\to(b,w')$ the arrows $u:a\to b$ of $I$ with $F(u)(w)=w'$. Let $D_z\subseteq I_z$ be the full subcategory on those pairs for which $w$ is degenerate, meaning that $w$ is the pullback of a lower-dimensional simplex along a noninjective surjective monotone map. Suppose that $N(I_z)$ is weakly contractible for every nondegenerate simplex $z$ of $K$, and that $N(D_z)\hookrightarrow N(I_z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every degenerate simplex $z$ of $K$. Then the pure-upper inclusion $N(I)\hookrightarrow K_F$ is right anodyne. Neither $K$ nor any $K_a$ is required to be a quasicategory; $I$ need not be a poset or directed, and the maps $\pi_a$ need not be injective.

proof.text: For a face-stable family $L_r\subseteq K_r$, include $N(I)$ and every simplex whose unique nondegenerate root in $K_F$ has nonempty lower block in $L$. The unique root exists by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], applied to $K_F$. These simplices form a simplicial subset: degeneracies preserve the root; taking faces deletes lower vertices, composes upper arrows, or removes a block, by [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones]. Passing from such a face to its root can remove lower degeneracies; choose the least element of each fiber of its monotone surjection to obtain a monotone section, so the new lower block is an iterated face of the original lower block. Removing upper degeneracies does not change the lower block. If the upper block disappears, any additional degeneracy of the resulting base simplex is removed by the same section argument. Face stability of $L$ therefore gives closure. This is precisely $L_F$ as a generated subset in [lem-coef-decomposition-simplex-attachment]: the specified generators and their degeneracies already form a simplicial subset.

source.place: Proof of HTT 4.2.3.8, first paragraph, printed p. 252; root and face-closure check expanded using Stacks 017R (lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets).

proof.text: Well-order each small set $K_m$ and then order $\coprod_{m\geq0}K_m$ first by dimension and then by these orders. Every proper face precedes its simplex. Thus its initial segments $L^\alpha$ are face-stable; every successor adds just one simplex $\sigma$, all of whose proper faces are old. Include ALL simplices of $K$, including degenerate ones: a nondegenerate lift can have a degenerate image. The subsets $L_F^\alpha$ start at $N(I)$ and end at $K_F$. At a limit their union equals the subset for the union of the initial segments, because membership is decided by the single lower simplex of a unique nondegenerate root. The ordinal is small since the disjoint union is small.

source.place: Proof of HTT 4.2.3.8, reduction to adding a single simplex, printed p. 252; explicit dimension-first ordering.

proof.text: Suppose the successor adds a nondegenerate $\sigma\in K_m$. Apply the nondegenerate clause of [lem-coef-decomposition-simplex-attachment] to $L=L^\alpha$, $L'=L^{\alpha+1}$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 2, and its lift category is exactly $I_\sigma$ in the statement. It expresses this successor inclusion as a pushout of $\partial\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)$. The given nondegenerate-simplex hypothesis says $N(I_\sigma)$ is weakly contractible. Hence [lem-coef-contractible-join-right-anodyne], with $A_0=\partial\Delta^m$, $A=\Delta^m$ and $B=N(I_\sigma)$, makes the attaching map right anodyne. This includes $m=0$.

source.place: Proof of HTT 4.2.3.8, nondegenerate case, using Lemma 4.2.3.6, printed pp. 251-252.

proof.text: Suppose instead that the successor adds a degenerate $\sigma\in K_m$. The degenerate clause of [lem-coef-decomposition-simplex-attachment] expresses it as a pushout of $P_\sigma\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)$, where $P_\sigma=(\partial\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma))\amalg_{\partial\Delta^m\star N(D_\sigma)}(\Delta^m\star N(D_\sigma))$. The nerve inclusion $N(D_\sigma)\hookrightarrow N(I_\sigma)$ is degreewise injective: a chain in the full subcategory is the same chain of objects and arrows in $I_\sigma$, by the nerve definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. It is a weak homotopy equivalence by the degenerate-simplex hypothesis. Both required inclusions are therefore degreewise injective. Apply [lem-coef-join-pushout-right-anodyne] with $A_0=\partial\Delta^m$, $A=\Delta^m$, $B_0=N(D_\sigma)$, $B=N(I_\sigma)$ to make the attaching map right anodyne. In particular, the pure lower simplex is already in $L_F^\alpha$ because its nondegenerate root has dimension less than $m$; the second summand of $P_\sigma$ retains that factor even when $D_\sigma$ is empty.

source.place: Proof of HTT 4.2.3.8, degenerate case, using Lemma 4.2.3.5, printed pp. 251-252.

proof.text: By [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], right anodyne maps are closed under pushouts, so Steps 3 and 4 make every successor inclusion right anodyne. The same definition closes this class under transfinite compositions. Apply it to the small continuous filtration in Step 2. Its composite is exactly $N(I)\hookrightarrow K_F$, which is therefore right anodyne. When $K$ is empty the composite is the identity of $N(I)$, also in the stated class.
